Choose Wallpaper Changer as your live wallpaper to turn it on. Until then the wallpaper keeps changing the usual way.
The album art of the song playing on Spotify, fading smoothly from one song to the next.
Shorter reacts faster, but Spotify may rate-limit below 20 s.

Uses Spotify\'s own session on this phone, so the wallpaper changes as the song does instead of up to a poll later, and asks Spotify far less often. Needs notification access, and only sees what plays on this phone: on another device it falls back to checking Spotify.
Drops the permanent notification and the background service: the wallpaper then follows only what plays on this phone, and stops following music played on other devices.
Wallpaper Changer talks to Spotify through a free developer app that you create once. It takes about two minutes.
1. Open the Spotify dashboard and log in.
2. Create an app. Under Redirect URIs add exactly:
3. Tick “Web API”, save, then paste the app’s Client ID here:
A Client ID has 32 letters and digits (0–9, a–f).
Spotify will ask you to allow access to what you are playing. Nothing else is read.
Sign-in didn’t finish. If Spotify said “Invalid redirect URI”, check that the dashboard has exactly: %1$s
While syncing, Android requires a notification. It shows the song on your wallpaper and has a Stop button. Without it the sync still works, just hidden.
Battery saving can stop the sync in the background. Let Wallpaper Changer run unrestricted: it only works while the screen is on.
On Samsung, also make sure it isn’t in Settings › Battery › Background usage limits › Sleeping apps.
Play something on Spotify: the wallpaper follows along. Turn it off any time from the app or from Quick Settings.
